comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: IWM sits long with a SELL divergence and the alignment column still says aligned, same for SPY short with HOLD. if aligned only means the side matches the multiplier sign and not the signal, the column is telling the reader nothing the Side column didn't already.

replies.author: Quantinvests
replies.body:
Good catch, and you’re right. “Aligned” just confirms the position is on the side the model picked, so it repeats what the Side column already tells you.

The Divergence column isn’t a trade instruction. It’s one opinion among several the model weighs. On IWM that opinion said sell, the rest outvoted it, so it stayed long. The next day the overall read turned negative and IWM flipped to a short. (Small correction: SPY shows SELL in that table; QQQ is the one at HOLD.)

If you want to see what was actually bought and sold each night, the Companion page has a Pipeline Trades tab. It lists every position that was added to, trimmed, flipped or closed, with the shares, prices and profit or loss. That’s where you’d see IWM’s flip.

See it here: [https://app.quantinvests.com/login?tour=1&next=%2Fcompanion%3Ftab%3Dtrades&utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social&utm\_campaign=reddit\_reply](https://app.quantinvests.com/login?tour=1&next=%2Fcompanion%3Ftab%3Dtrades&utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=reddit_reply)

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: then the useful column is the vote itself, how many of the opinions sided with the position, so the reader can see IWM was long on a split vote the day before it flipped. an outvoted sell that wins the next day is what the table should make visible, and right now it's what the table hides.

replies.author: Quantinvests
replies.body:
Right now, the table flattens the multi-factor ensemble output into a binary directional state, which obscures the underlying consensus distribution (e.g., whether a node is clearing on a unanimous 8/0 vector or a contested 5/3 split). Exposing that granular vote distribution on the companion view is definitely on the radar.

**How the Model Weightings Work:**

**Multiplier Scaling:** The architecture computes and dynamically scales the weightings of the 8 constituent multipliers based on positive return contributions (rewarding predictive alpha) and penalizes them during adverse drift.

**ML Feature Optimization:** The meta-model's internal feature weights are not static; they continuously adapt via online and offline training loops, re-evaluating the covariance and predictive efficacy of each signal as new market regime data flows through the pipeline.

**Target Definition (Dependent Variable):** The ensemble optimizes against a explicit forward-looking dependent variable—typically the next-period risk-adjusted return, residual alpha, or a directional classification target (y).

If you go to the bottom of the divergence page it looks at the dependent vs index etfs. I measure it against 13 sectors, one volatility and one currency. Also takes into account the correlation, so if the dependencies change so will the sign.

[https://app.quantinvests.com/divergence](https://app.quantinvests.com/divergence)

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the 8/0 versus 5/3 split is the column I'd read, yes. one step further and it becomes useful: next to each split, how often a call at that split was right over the last few months. a contested 5/3 that wins as often as a unanimous 8/0 tells the reader the vote count is decoration; a gap tells them when to trust it.
